23.33.0.en: Paradise of the Fathers: "Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast" [34].

23.33.1.en: The drunkard resembles a man lying down in the midst of the waves of the sea, or resting his head on the top of a mast; he will find no rest and feel no security, although he often justifies his resort to drunkenness as an escape from the problems and troubles that pursue him.

23.33.2.en: He says: "They have stricken me, and I was not sick.

23.33.3.en: They have beaten me, and I felt it not.

23.34.0.en: When shall I awake? I will seek it yet again" [35].

23.34.1.en: * The early Fathers found the drinking of wine very hard, because it makes the old men like children without knowledge, and stirs in the young men an inclination to evil desire, and the ascetics hate it because of the grievous war of fornication.

23.34.2.en: * Abba Isaiah was asked: "If a brother compels me to drink a cup of wine with him in his cell, is it good for me to go with him?" He answered: "Flee from the drinking of wine, and you will be safe as the gazelle is safe from the beast. For many, because of this matter, have been driven to fall through their thoughts."

23.34.3.en: Paradise of the Fathers: * Do not love wine, lest it deprive you of the good pleasure of God. Love the poor, that you may be delivered in the time of distress.

23.34.4.en: St. Abba Moses the Black: * When we are struck with blindness we cannot see in ourselves anything but grave offenses, supposing that we need only be clean of those offenses alone which the laws of the world condemn. And if we see that we have been freed from them for a while, we think that we have become entirely without sin... So we do not see the many stains that gather together within us, and consequently we do not remove them by saving contrition, nor do we grieve when thoughts of vainglory befall us, nor do we weep over our prayers which we offer in great slackness and lukewarmness. Nor do we count the wandering of our mind during the chanting of the Psalms and prayers as a fault. Nor are we ashamed of our imaginations of many things which we would be ashamed to utter or practice before men, and which are laid bare before the divine sight. Nor do we cleanse the corruption of defiled dreams with abundant tears... Nor do we believe that any loss befalls us when we forget God, thinking of corrupt earthly things. Thus the words of Solomon apply to us: "They have stricken me, and I was not sick; they have beaten me, and I felt it not."

23.34.5.en: Abba Theonas: * I am not presenting to you my own opinion, but I recall the opinion of the blessed Anthony, with which he put to shame the sloth of a certain monk who was overcome by indifference... When a man came to him and said that this order of asceticism was not perfect, declaring that he sought a greater virtue for man, practicing what belongs to the perfect life alone in a manner beyond what is fitting for the dwellers of the wilderness, then the blessed Anthony asked him about the place where he lived, and when he told him that he lived with his relatives, boasting of their help to him, freed from every care and daily labor, devoting his life to reading and prayer without ceasing and without distraction of spirit, at once the blessed Anthony said to him: Tell me, my dear friend, do you grieve at their griefs and misfortunes, and rejoice at their joys?

23.34.6.en: The man confessed that he shared with them in that, then the elder said to him: "You must know that you will be judged in the world to come for the community with which you live, thus sharing with them in their gain and loss, their joy and sorrow"...

23.34.7.en: And when he was not persuaded by this, the blessed Anthony went on to say: This kind of life and this indifference not only drive you to the loss mentioned before, even though you do not feel it now, as it is written in the Book of Proverbs: "They have stricken me, and I was not sick; they have beaten me, and I felt it not" (Prov 35:23), and as it is said in the prophet: "Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knoweth it not: yea, gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not" (Hos 9:7), but they also draw your mind unceasingly toward temporal things, and change it according to circumstances. Likewise, as they offer you the fruit of their hands and supply you with provisions, they thereby deprive you of carrying out the commandment of the blessed Apostle, for when he gave his last charge to the leaders of the Church of Ephesus he assured them that, despite his being occupied with his holy duties of preaching the Gospel, he was working for his own needs and the needs of those who were with him in the ministry, saying: "Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me" (Acts 34:20). And that you may see how he did this as an example for us, he says in another place: "For yourselves know how ye ought to follow us: for we behaved not ourselves disorderly among you... Not because we have not power, but to make ourselves an ensample unto you to follow us" (2 Thess 7:3, 9).

23.34.8.en: Abba Abraham: * Those whom sexual desire assails and overcomes must break the earthly bonds, for when they are occupied with them immoderately, they are not aware of the arrows of sin that may pierce them. Therefore the drunken man, who has lost consciousness, says by the tongue of the prophet Solomon: "They have stricken me, and I was not sick; they have beaten me, and I felt it not: when shall I awake? I will seek it yet again" (Prov 23:35).

23.34.9.en: The mind rests and sleeps without any cares to trouble it, and feels no pain, even when it is struck. This happens when it cannot see before it the evils that surround it, nor is it aware of those it has committed. Evils crowd upon this soul, and it does not feel the allurements of vices, nor does it even want to rise to defend itself. At the same time it wishes to be awake only in order to find wine again. That is, being weighed down with a weak and wavering sleep that does not allow it to watch over itself and guard itself, it tries to awake only to plunge into the cares of this world and be drunk with its pleasures.

23.34.10.en: It sleeps at the time when it ought to be awake and watchful, and when it awakes it does not pursue what it ought, but other worldly matters. For this reason it was written before: "Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast" (Prov 23:34).

23.34.11.en: The man who neglects the wars of iniquities that rise against him, as though they were waves beating against mountain peaks, sleeps heavily in the midst of a sea of worldly trials.

23.34.13.en: Grant me to become in Your image!

23.34.14.en: * Sitting with rulers calls for reverence and attentiveness; let me sit at Your feet, O King of kings, and listen to Your sweet voice.

23.34.15.en: Let me enjoy the table of Your love, and long for Your eternal goods.

23.34.16.en: The world with all its pleasures becomes tasteless, for the sweetness of eternity surrounds me.

23.34.17.en: * My soul is broken within me as I sit with You at Your table.

23.34.18.en: You host me, and give me Your Body and Blood as food for my soul!

23.34.19.en: What love is greater than this!

23.34.20.en: * I will not sit with Your holy Book without You, for You are the Word of God who satisfies souls.

23.34.21.en: Your Holy Spirit is the giver of enlightenment.

23.34.22.en: I see You transfigured in Your Book, I draw from the overflow of Your glory, and my whole being is drawn toward Your heavens.

23.34.23.en: * When my soul is satisfied, gluttony flees from me.

23.34.24.en: I see life as better than food.

23.34.25.en: I eat that I may live, and I do not live that I may eat!

23.34.26.en: Life with You has its delight!

23.34.27.en: * Grant me, with Daniel and his companions, not to desire the delicacies of this world, so that Your wisdom becomes my desired food.

23.34.28.en: Grant me not to spoil my energy with greed and the love of riches, so that wealth does not become a god to me in place of You.

23.34.29.en: * Give me the wings of a dove, that I may fly and be with You in heaven.

23.34.30.en: Lest my heart be absorbed in the love of possessions, and every possession fly away, and I lose my life!

23.34.31.en: * Grant me to love everyone, yet not to enter into fellowship with an envious man, nor to share his feasts and delicacies.

23.34.32.en: Grant me friendships with spiritual people, that I may cleave to You the more, and learn much from them.

23.34.33.en: I see You transfigured in my friendship with Your children.

23.34.34.en: Embrace me with them in Your bosom.

23.34.35.en: * Teach me with whom to speak and give counsel, and when to speak, and what to say.

23.34.36.en: For I fear for myself, lest I be a lover of teaching and of much talking.

23.34.37.en: Grant me the spirit of discernment, O heavenly Wisdom of God!

23.34.38.en: * May You shine with the light of Your knowledge in my depths.

23.34.39.en: I know You, my Creator and Savior, and I know my weakness, so I cleave to You!

23.34.40.en: I know my sin, so I flee to You, O Forgiver of sins.

23.34.41.en: * Let Your hand be stretched out and discipline me, but do not deliver me to death.

23.34.42.en: There is none who loves me like You, and none who cares for my salvation and my eternity like You.

23.34.43.en: Count me as a little child, in need of Your fatherhood and tenderness, and in need of Your chastisements.

23.34.44.en: * If the hearts of our fathers rejoice in our wisdom, and their inmost parts exult in the uprightness of our life, how much more are You pleased with us, O heavenly Father, wonderful in Your love?

23.34.45.en: * Fix Your fear in my flesh, that I may walk in what pleases You, and turn aside from all that You do not desire.

23.34.46.en: I long for Your eternal Kingdom, and I seek no temporal glory!

23.34.47.en: My soul rejoices as it hopes to depart to You.

23.34.48.en: And it is not entangled in the troubles and cares of life.

23.34.49.en: Let me always enjoy Your victory, and delight in the answer to my petitions.

23.34.50.en: * Let me walk by Your Spirit with commitment, and be drunk with Your Spirit, not with the wine of the world.

23.34.51.en: * My holy Savior, in humility You obeyed St. Mary Your mother and Joseph the carpenter.

23.34.52.en: Grant me to share in Your obedience.

23.34.53.en: Grant me to be girded with truth, and to walk in wisdom, discipline, and understanding.

23.34.54.en: * Lord, receive my heart, engrave Your law upon it, and establish Your Kingdom in it.

23.34.55.en: Let no base desire draw near to it, and no evil pleasure attract it.

24.0.s.en: 1. A warning against envying the wicked

24.0.0.en: 1 Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them. 2 For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.

24.0.1.en: Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them [1].

24.0.2.en: The success and arrogance of the wicked have often raised questions in some about divine justice, and have sometimes even stirred people's envy and jealousy of them, as though brute force were always above the right, injustice above justice, and darkness stronger than light. It is no wonder, then, that it is said: "But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped. For I was envious at the arrogant, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked. For there are no bands in their death: but their body is fat. They are not in trouble as other men; neither are they plagued like other men. Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain; violence covereth them as a garment. Their eyes stand out with fatness: they have more than heart could wish. They scoff and speak wickedly concerning oppression: they speak loftily. They set their mouth against the heavens, and their tongue walketh through the earth" (Ps 73:1-9). But the psalmist discovered that the wicked are "like the green herb" that soon wither (Ps 37:1). This the Holy Scripture confirms and repeats again and again; we content ourselves here with the following passages:

24.0.3.en: "The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor" (Job 15:20).

24.0.4.en: "The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor: let them be taken in the devices that they have imagined" (Ps 10:2).

24.0.5.en: "Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil man: seek out his wickedness till thou find none" (Ps 10:15).

24.0.6.en: "Many sorrows shall be to the wicked: but he that trusteth in the LORD, mercy shall compass him about" (Ps 32:10).

24.0.7.en: "Evil shall slay the wicked: and they that hate the righteous shall be punished" (Ps 34:21).

24.0.8.en: "For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: yea, thou shalt diligently consider his place, and it shall not be" (Ps 37:10).

24.0.9.en: "The curse of the LORD is in the house of the wicked: but he blesseth the habitation of the just" (Prov 3:33).

24.0.10.en: "His own iniquities shall take the wicked himself, and he shall be holden with the cords of his sins" (Prov 5:22).

24.0.11.en: "As the whirlwind passeth, so is the wicked no more: but the righteous is an everlasting foundation" (Prov 10:25).

24.0.12.en: "The righteousness of the perfect shall direct his way: but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness" (Prov 11:5).

24.0.13.en: "The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead" (Prov 11:8).

24.0.14.en: "The wicked earns the wages of deceit, but to him that soweth righteousness, the wages of faithfulness" (Prov 11:18).

24.0.15.en: "A wicked soul destroys him who has it, and makes him a laughingstock to his enemies" (Sir 6:4).

24.0.16.en: "The eye of the covetous man is not satisfied with his portion, and the injustice of the wicked wearies his soul" (Sir 14:9).

24.0.17.en: "Are there yet in the house of the wicked the treasures of wickedness, and the scant measure that is accursed?" (Mic 6:10).

24.0.18.en: * ["But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped. For I was envious at the arrogant, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked" (Ps 73:2-3).]

24.0.19.en: What brought him near to slipping was his envy of the ungodly, when he saw the doers of good and those committed to justice in a narrow living, hardship, and distress, while the wicked and malicious were in comfortable living, in ease and delight, so that even in their death there is nothing that troubles or distresses them. And if sickness comes upon them, their pain is light and not severe as it comes upon the good and those of virtue.

24.0.20.en: Father Anthimus of Jerusalem: * I observed the sinners, and I found them in peace (Ps 73:3).

24.0.21.en: What peace? A temporary, worldly, dissolute, and earthly peace.

24.0.22.en: I saw those who do not serve God receiving what I desire in order to serve God, and my feet slipped, and my steps had almost slipped...

24.0.23.en: Observe that these men are proud and undisciplined; observe that the ox is prepared for slaughter and is allowed to sin freely, and to break what it wants until the day of its slaughter comes.

24.1.0.en: St. Augustine: For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief [2].

24.1.1.en: The first fruit of evil is the corruption of the heart, as it turns to violence and the love of plunder, so that true love does not dwell in it, and consequently it is unable to see God, the divine Love! Evil corrupts the heart and the lips are corrupted with it, so that if they utter sweet words they are mixed with the poison of mischief, that is, of evil. Their wicked tongues often reveal what their hearts hide of evils toward others.

24.2.0.en: 3 Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established: 4 And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches. 5 A wise man is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength. 6 For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors there is safety. 7 Wisdom is too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate. 8 He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person. 9 The thought of foolishness is sin: and the scorner is an abomination to men. 10 If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.

24.2.1.en: Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established [3].

24.2.2.en: If the Lord Christ is the wisdom of God, then our spiritual house is founded on the Lord Christ, the true Wisdom.

24.2.3.en: The building of the house of wisdom continues in this life until we reach our heavenly Jerusalem, so the wise, the learners, and the understanding do not cease seeking more.

24.2.4.en: St. Hippolytus calls on us to build walls around wisdom so that it may stand and not be shattered.

24.2.5.en: * Open the door of Your treasure to us, O Lord, when we offer the prayers of our supplications. Let our prayers serve as an ambassador for us, reconciling us with the Godhead.

24.2.6.en: O all you wise, take heed; O you learners, seek understanding and knowledge, for you are learners and wise.

24.2.7.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian: * Fence it about with holy thoughts, for you need a greater defense, since there are many things that threaten such a possession with dangers. But if we are able to fortify it, if there are virtues within our power that increase the knowledge of God, these will be bulwarks for it, such as practice of it, study, and the whole chain of virtues.

24.2.8.en: St. Hippolytus: * If anyone wishes to understand the houses as good works, then every good work is the house of its owner. Those who hear the words of Jesus and do them... build their foundation upon the rock (Mt 7:24). Since virtue as a whole is one, he who strives in it builds his house, setting it upon the rock, upon the word of God who is not defeated, that is, upon Christ.

24.2.9.en: St. Didymus the Blind: * (Solomon) calls Christ wisdom and understanding. And the house is the Church (of Christ) which He builds, and He fills its storehouses with every kind of precious and splendid wealth; its storehouses are the hearts of those who believe in Christ and live in imitation of Him. These hearts abound with goodness in thoughts, words, and deeds. For this reason they are made worthy of eternal blessedness.

24.3.0.en: St. John Chrysostom: And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches [4].

24.3.1.en: God, who is all-wise, created man in His image and likeness so that he might build his inner being, especially his mind, emotions, and feelings, upon divine wisdom, true knowledge, and the truth of the Gospel, so that the holy temple of the Lord is established within him. And his depths are turned into a storehouse bearing the treasures of knowledge that cannot be valued! As our teacher the Apostle James says: "But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy. And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace" (Jas 3:17-18).

24.3.2.en: St. Jerome sees that everything diminishes with time, even spiritual practices such as asceticism, fasts, moving from one place to another to seek spiritual benefit, hospitality to strangers and giving, and perseverance in prayer; for as the body grows weak with advancing age these exercises lessen, but wisdom increases always and is not broken by advancing age.

24.3.3.en: The person who clings to divine wisdom does not fear time, nor illness, nor the unknown future; he is in constant growth in wisdom, discernment, learning, and knowledge, increasing in radiance and light, and even in inner strength and authority.

24.3.4.en: * This is the discernment which is called not only "the light of the body" but also "the sun," as the Apostle says: "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath" (Eph 4:26). It is also called "authority," since Scripture does not permit us to do anything without it: "He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls" (Prov 25:28).

24.3.5.en: And in it wisdom dwells, and understanding and knowledge reside, and without it our inner house is not built, and we cannot gather the spiritual wealth that is ours, for it is said: "Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established: and by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches" (Prov 24:3-4).

24.3.6.en: And it is the "perfect food" on which the perfect feed in growth and health, for it is said: "But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil" (Heb 5:14).

24.3.7.en: And its importance and necessity for us appear in proportion to the importance of the word of God and its power, for it is said: "For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart" (Heb 4:12).

24.4.0.en: Abba Moses: A wise man is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength [5].

24.5.0.en: For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors there is safety [6].

24.5.1.en: If wisdom is the foundation for building the inner house, and is the precious treasure of the soul, then it is also the secret of the soul's true dignity and strength, as it is behind victory and salvation. The wise believer is in constant war against the devil and his hosts, resisting them with heavenly wisdom, and with humility in the counsel and direction of his spiritual fathers.

24.5.2.en: * Perhaps (Solomon) warns us not to rush into war without deliberation. He says: Look, when you take a decision, is it not profitable that wisdom be in the midst of the matters?

24.5.3.en: St. John Chrysostom: Wisdom is too high for a fool.

24.6.0.en: He openeth not his mouth in the gate [7].

24.6.1.en: The foolish man, who persists in his evil, does not accept counsel and is unable to attain wisdom. Therefore when the time comes for his trial before the divine court (justice was administered at the gates of the cities), he is silent, he openeth not his mouth in the gate, for he has nothing with which to justify his folly. He is like one who enters the wedding without a wedding garment, and when he was asked about it he "was speechless" (Mt 12:22). "Then said the king to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth" (Mt 22:13).

24.6.2.en: How wonderful! Because of our folly we stand at the gate silent, unable to justify ourselves; so the Word of God Himself came incarnate, and He, the Holy and Righteous One, entered in our place to be tried, bearing our sins. "He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth" (Isa 53:7). He kept silent to give us Himself, that we may speak by Him, and be counted before the Father as righteous, with the right to enter His throne!

24.6.3.en: When we are summoned, not to the gate of the city for trial before the men of justice, but to the gate of the great judgment, we cannot open our mouths to defend ourselves. But thanks be to the Lamb of God, who did not open His mouth at His trial, that the gates of heaven may be opened before us on the great day of the Lord.

24.6.4.en: * By the Cross He paid our debts.

24.6.5.en: By the Cross He gladdened Paradise, whose closed gates were opened.

24.6.6.en: By the Cross He shut the gates of Hades and its bars, that those who believe in Him might not enter it.

24.6.7.en: By the Cross He crushed the ancient serpent, and made void its deceit.

24.6.8.en: By the Cross He restored to woman her dignity.

24.6.9.en: By the Cross the evil times came to an end, and the joyful age of grace was opened.

24.6.10.en: By the Cross He removed from Adam and Eve and their descendants the garments of shame, and gave them the garment of surpassing glory.

24.7.0.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh: He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person [8].

24.8.0.en: The thought of foolishness is sin: and the scorner is an abomination to men [9].

24.8.1.en: Since wisdom plays the role of builder of the spiritual house [2], and grants wealth, dignity, strength, victory, and salvation (5-6), folly or evil, on the contrary, demolishes, corrupts, and causes ridicule. Man loses his spiritual, moral, social, and eternal being. He becomes a corrupt leaven, corrupting whoever clings to him or mingles with him. And he emits the odor of death, loathsome and foolish.

24.8.2.en: The fool treats the Holy One and His holy things lightly, like Pharaoh who asked scornfully: "Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice?" (Ex 5:2). And as Belshazzar the king of Babylon did, who, "whiles he tasted the wine, commanded to bring the golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem; that the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, might drink therein... They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone" (Dan 5:2-4). And since the fool treats the Holy One and holy things lightly, he himself becomes an object of ridicule, even before himself, as happened with Belshazzar, for "the king's countenance was changed, and his thoughts troubled him, so that the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees smote one against another" (Dan 5:6).

24.8.3.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa sees that the difference between wisdom and folly is exactly like the difference between light and darkness. Darkness in truth has no being, but is the absence of light; so folly has no being, but is a deprivation of wisdom. Evil has no being, but is the absence of goodness.

24.8.4.en: * There is nothing in common between the wise person and the fool, whether in human expressions or in divine rewards. For in human works the end surprises all, while they think they are still at the beginning. But the destiny of the wise person will not share in the portion of the fool.

24.8.5.en: St. Gregory the Wonderworker: * Darkness is folly, through which we fall into sin, not seeing the truth. And knowledge is the light we obtain, which makes ignorance vanish, and also grants us pure vision.

24.9.0.en: St. Clement of Alexandria: If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small [10].

24.9.1.en: The day of adversity is the thermometer that reveals to man the truth of his strength. For the wise man, the man of God, may faint with Elijah the prophet, who "requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers" (1 Kgs 19:4). But the hand of God raised him up, and God entered into a dialogue with him, and his life at that time ended with his ascent to heaven in a chariot of fire. But as for the fool, adversity exposes the truth of his weakness, and the man himself drives himself to ruin.

24.9.2.en: He who thinks of evil or folly has taken part in sin, if not in deed or word, then in thought. This participation corrupts a man's mind and heart, and even his life.

24.9.3.en: * The knowledge of evil is not blamed; rather, participation in evil is blamed.

24.10.0.en: 11 If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain; 12 If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?

24.10.1.en: Deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain.

24.10.3.en: The wise man did not ask us to examine those who are led to death, for that is the work of judges and rulers. But if an opportunity is found to rescue someone from death, or from distress, we must not refrain from the work of love.

24.10.4.en: He did not specify the nationality of those whom we rescue in their distress, nor their religion, nor their conduct, since we ought to support all mankind with wisdom and love as much as we can.

24.10.5.en: * (Solomon) did not say: "Inquire out of curiosity, and find out who these are." Yet most of those led to death are wicked. This is love in general. For he who does good to a friend does it not for God's sake, but he who does good to one he does not know does it for God alone.

24.10.6.en: St. John Chrysostom: * You must therefore learn compassion for those in distress, and not terrify those exposed to the danger of deadly despair, nor burden them with harsh words, but correct them with quiet, deep words of consolation. For wise Solomon says: "Deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain. Forbear not" (Prov 24:11). And be like our Savior: "A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench..." (Mt 21:20).

24.10.7.en: Abba Moses: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it?

24.11.0.en: And shall not he render to every man according to his works? [12].

24.11.1.en: These two verses point to a person's obligation to rescue the innocent man as long as it is within his power. It was among the common customs in Syria and Palestine at that time that when one of the criminals was taken to trial, a herald would go before him on the road announcing his crime, so that if anyone had information in favor of this accused person, he would come forward. If someone came forward, the person's trial would be reopened in the court, and his case file opened anew. If someone withheld a true piece of information that could acquit the person, he was counted as one who had killed him, because he hid from the court a truth and caused the person to be put to death unjustly.

24.11.2.en: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, the Samaritan cared for the wounded Jew and saved him from death, while the priest and the Levite were counted as having committed a crime against this wounded man, because they did not care to rescue him.

24.11.3.en: This concerns those led to bodily death; how much more is the responsibility of the believer when he sees millions of souls exposed to eternal destruction in the fire of Gehenna, and does not come forward to pray, fast, or counsel for their rescue; rather he shares with Cain the murderer of his brother, saying: "Am I my brother's keeper?"

24.11.4.en: * (The Lord) teaches us that the man who went down (from Jerusalem to Jericho) was neighbor only to the one who wished to keep the commandments and prepare himself to be a neighbor to everyone who needs help.

24.11.5.en: Origen: * Some think that their neighbor is their brother, from their family, from their relatives.

24.11.6.en: Our Lord teaches us who the neighbor is, in the Gospel, in the parable of the man who went down from Jerusalem to Jericho... Everyone is our neighbor, so we must not harm anyone... We are neighbors, all people are neighbors to all people, because we have one Father.

24.12.0.en: 13 My son, eat thou honey, because it is good; and the honeycomb, which is sweet to thy taste: 14 So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul: when thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.

24.12.1.en: My son, eat thou honey, because it is good; and the honeycomb, which is sweet to thy taste [13].

24.12.2.en: Honey of the bees was among the sweetest foods to the Jews, and Solomon used it to warn us against the honeyed words of the adulteress (Prov 5:3). Again, the praise others give a man is counted as honey, which if we eat much of it burdens the stomach (Prov 25:27). Solomon also calls us to moderation in everything, for he who eats too much honey has his stomach stuffed and vomits it (Prov 25:16). He whose soul is satisfied has no need of, and cannot bear, the honey of men's praise of him (Prov 27:7).

24.12.3.en: The unfaithful woman's lips drop honey, but whoever unites with her is led by her to the ways of bitter death. But the Lord Christ carries us with Him on the way of the Cross, and leads us to the joy of His resurrection and its glories.

24.12.4.en: There is no sweetness for the soul better than divine wisdom, for it was said of the Lord Christ, the wisdom of God: "His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely" (Song 5:16), and it was said of Him, "and the desire of all nations shall come" (Hag 2:7).

24.12.5.en: * The Lord Jesus knows how the soul of man, that is, the rational mind created in His image, cannot be satisfied except by Him alone...

24.12.6.en: He knows that He has been revealed and that He is hidden. He knows that in Him what is hidden has been declared. He knows all this. The Psalm says: "How great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord, which thou hast hid for them that fear thee, which thou hast wrought for them that hope in thee" (Ps 31:19) LXX.

24.12.7.en: Your sweetness is great and manifold, which You have hidden for those who fear You...

24.12.8.en: To whom will You open it? To those who hope in You.

24.12.9.en: A two-sided question has been raised, but each side resolves the other...

24.12.10.en: Are those who fear and those who hope different?

24.12.11.en: Are not those who fear God the very ones who hope in Him...?

24.12.12.en: To the Law belongs fear, and to grace hope... The Law warns the one who relies on himself, and grace helps the one who trusts in God... We hear the Law. If there is no grace, you hear the punishment that comes upon you... Let him cry out: "O wretched man that I am!" (Rom 7:24). Know yourself as defeated, let your strength be in shame, and say: "O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?"... Thus the Law warns the one who relies on himself.

24.12.13.en: Look, here is a man relying on himself, trying to strive; he is prostrate, enslaved, and taken captive. Whoever has learned to rely on God, while the Law continued to warn him not to rely on himself, is now upheld by grace, as he relies on God. In this confidence he says: "Who shall deliver me from the body of this death? The grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord" (Rom 7:24-25) [Vulgate].

24.12.14.en: Now look at the sweetness, taste it, delight in it. Hear the Psalm: "Taste and see how sweet the Lord is" (Ps 34:8) [Vulgate]. He becomes sweet to you, as He delivers you.

24.12.15.en: You were in the bitterness of yourself, when you relied on yourself. Drink the sweetness, and receive thus the zeal of the great abundance.

24.12.16.en: St. Augustine: So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul.

24.13.0.en: When thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off [14].

24.13.1.en: He who possesses the Lord Christ, the wisdom of God, enjoys the eternal inheritance and fellowship in glory; his hope is not cut off.

24.13.2.en: * Since it comes to this, that one must take everything from within the river or the valley, and rejoice in it, we say that our Lord Jesus Christ is compared to a river, in whom we find every delight and enjoyment in hope, and in whom we rejoice with a spiritual, divine joy.

24.13.3.en: St. Cyril the Great: * How wretched I am?!

24.13.4.en: My God... when will this corrupt nature leave me, and Your perfect power work in me?!

24.13.5.en: My God... how delightful are solitude, stillness, truth, and purity, all of which are Yours! But I amuse myself with noise, clamor, vanity, and vice!

24.13.6.en: I return, and what more shall I say?! You are the true Good, merciful, holy, just... but I am wicked, self-loving, sinful, unjust...!

24.13.7.en: You are the light, but I am darkness!

24.13.8.en: You are life, but I am death!

24.13.9.en: You are the Physician, but I am sick!

24.13.10.en: You are joy, but I am sorrow!

24.13.11.en: You are the true Truth, but I am real vanity, like any man on earth!

24.13.12.en: In what language do You want me to speak to You, my Creator?! I beseech You to be pleased to listen to me. I am the work of Your hands, and my destruction is a fearful thing!

24.13.13.en: I am Your creature, and behold I die! I am the work of Your hands, and behold I slide down toward nothingness!

24.13.14.en: If I have existence, You are the One who gave me existence, "Thy hands have made me and fashioned me" (Ps 119:73). Your hands that were nailed to the Cross, let them give me peace; for will You despise the work of Your hands?!

24.13.15.en: Ah! I look upon Your deep wounds, for You have engraved my name in Your hands! Read my name and save me!

24.13.16.en: My soul that groans before You is the work of Your hands. Create in me a new creature; this is Your work. Therefore it does not cease to cry out to You, saying: "O Life, give me life again!"

24.13.17.en: It is the clay of Your hands, wrapping itself around You, beseeching You to restore to it its first beauty!

24.13.18.en: Forgive me, my God, since You have permitted me to speak with You. For who is man that he should speak with the Lord his Creator?!

24.13.19.en: Yes. Forgive me! Forgive my boldness! Forgive Your servant who dared to raise his voice before his Master!

24.13.20.en: Necessity knows no law! Pain drives me to speak with You! The calamity that has befallen me makes me call the Physician because I am sick! I seek the light because I am blind! I search for life because I am dead! And who is this Physician, Light, and Life but You?!

24.13.21.en: O Jesus of Nazareth, have mercy on me!

24.14.0.en: 15 Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place: 16 For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief. 17 Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth: 18 Lest the LORD see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him. 19 Fret not thyself because of evil men, neither be thou envious at the wicked; 20 For there shall be no reward to the evil man; the candle of the wicked shall be put out. 21 My son, fear thou the LORD and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change: 22 For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?

24.14.1.en: Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the dwelling of the righteous.

24.14.3.en: What is the dwelling of the righteous but the divine embrace? And what is his resting place, his true place of repose, but fellowship with God? The wicked lies in wait for the righteous, setting many snares for him, that the righteous may fall into one of them, and not return to the divine embrace, and lose his fellowship with God. The wicked finds his pleasure in leading the righteous astray, and in ruining his own soul by falling with him into iniquity.

24.14.4.en: This statement seems addressed to the wicked, that he may not lie in wait to catch the righteous, for he toils in vain, because God is the defender of the righteous and his savior. But since the wicked does not listen to the voice of God, the address is in truth directed to the righteous, that he may not fear the wicked nor be troubled by him, whatever his plans and resources, because God Himself fortifies His children against the wicked and their evil deeds.

24.14.5.en: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again.

24.15.0.en: But the wicked shall fall into mischief [16].

24.15.1.en: If the wicked exert all their effort to catch the righteous in the snare of evil, then God for His part opens the doors of hope before mankind, so that everyone who falls, however many times he falls, may seek salvation and find it in his hands. But the wicked, who exerts all his effort to lay stumbling blocks before the righteous, himself stumbles, while the righteous are saved and crowned.

24.15.2.en: * The words "seven times" are used to express every kind of affliction by which a man collapses in the eyes of men. And the words "riseth up again" mean that the man benefits from all these afflictions.

24.15.3.en: * When evils come upon the wicked they fall by them. And when evils come upon the righteous, God strengthens them, and raises up all those who have fallen (Ps 145:14), all who belong to Him, for "God resisteth the proud" (Jas 4:6).

24.15.4.en: St. Augustine: * By the help of God we can and must not commit grave sins, but there is no righteous person who does not sin, and we will not be able to live without little sins. We are always disturbed and tormented by these sins as by flying insects buzzing around us. Often sins creep in through thoughts, desires, conversations, or actions, as something unavoidable, through weakness and because of forgetfulness, if a man thinks of grave sins. Therefore we must not make light of our sins because they are small, but let us fear them because they are many. Drops of rain are small, but because they are many they fill rivers and flood houses, and sometimes by their force move mountains.

24.15.5.en: Father Caesarius, Bishop of Arles: * A Christian is said to "rise up" in two senses: the first is when he is freed in this world by grace from the death of vices, and continues justified by God, and as the great Solomon in wisdom said: "A just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again." The second is in the general resurrection, where the righteous enjoys the eternal rewards.

24.15.6.en: Cassiodorus: * This speaking of the forgetting of former sins, I mean the principal sins condemned by the Mosaic Law, the inclination to which has ended and has been removed from us by a good life, and for which repentance has been completed. But as for the other (lesser) offenses, of which it was said: "For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again" (Prov 24:16), repentance for them does not end, because whether through ignorance or forgetfulness or thought or speech or mere desire or necessity or weakness of the flesh or uncleanness in a dream... into these things we often fall every day without our will or with it. For such sins David the prophet prays to the Lord, and asks to be cleansed from them and forgiven for them: "Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults" (Ps 19:12). And the Apostle also says: "For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do" (Rom 7:19). Therefore he sighed, saying: "O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?" (Rom 7:24).

24.15.7.en: We fall into these sins easily as though by the very nature of things, so that despite our alertness and watchfulness toward them, we cannot avoid them altogether. This is what made one of the disciples whom Jesus loved cry out, saying: "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us" (1 Jn 1:8).

24.16.0.en: Father Pinufius: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth [17].

24.16.1.en: It befits the believer to be after the pattern of God, who maketh His sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust. Let the believer's heart be widened with love even toward those who oppose him.

24.16.2.en: The Apostle Paul says: "For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son" (Rom 5:10). If God reconciled us after we bore a spirit of enmity against Him, let us return this love to Him in those whom He loves, that is, in all mankind.

24.16.3.en: Whoever rejoices at his enemy's fall and whose heart is glad at his stumbling is counted as an opponent of God Himself, who seeks the salvation of all.

24.16.4.en: * He who rejoices in the misfortunes of others grieves God, as Solomon says. In any case, the Jews were not rejected for the sake of the Gentiles, but rather because they refused to give the Gospel the opportunity to be preached to the Gentiles. If you boast against those in whose root you were grafted, you insult the people who received you so that you might turn from evil to good. You will not continue in this if you were grafted in and remain firm in it.

24.17.0.en: Father Ambrosiaster: Lest the LORD see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him [18].

24.17.1.en: The eyes of the Lord observe what is in our hearts, and if He sees in a heart joy at the calamities and disasters that befall another, God's wrath turns from the one under discipline to the one who gloats over him, as happened with the sons of Edom who gloated over Israel after their captivity, and the prophet Obadiah recorded his book especially because of this attitude, to highlight the gravity of gloating over those on whom discipline falls. "But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; neither shouldest thou have spoken proudly in the day of distress. Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity; yea, thou shouldest not have looked on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance in the day of their calamity; neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape; neither shouldest thou have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress. For the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head" (Obad 12-15).

24.17.2.en: * We must not be puffed up by our victory, therefore he warns us, saying: "Lest when thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and dwelt therein; and when thy herds and thy flocks multiply, and thy silver and thy gold is multiplied, and all that thou hast is multiplied; then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the LORD thy God, which brought thee forth... from the house of bondage (sin)" (Deut 8:12-14). Likewise Solomon says in Proverbs: "Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth (that is, at your victory over sin and Satan), and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth: lest the LORD see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him" (Prov 24:17-18), that is, lest God see the pride of your heart and no longer attack him (defend you against sin), and thereby forsake you, so that the lust you had previously overcome by the grace of God overcomes you.
